drivingQuestion: Is contemplation tantamount to speech, and what does the mishna's ruling that a ba'al keri contemplates Shema show about it?
outcomeNote: Ravina and Rav Hisda draw opposite inferences from the mishna and each is defended; the final difficulty against Rav Adda is resolved by the Torah/rabbinic distinction, but the contemplation question itself is not decided.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רָבִינָא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי. דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי — לָמָּה מְהַרְהֵר?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Ravina said: That is to say,» from the mishna that «contemplation is tantamount to speech. As if it would enter your mind» that «it is not tantamount to speech,» then «why» does one who is impure because of a seminal emission «contemplate?» It must be that it is tantamount to speech.

segments.he: אֶלָּא מַאי — הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי, יוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו?
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this: «But what» are you saying, that «contemplation is tantamount to speech?» Then, if one who is impure because of a seminal emission is permitted to contemplate, why does he not «utter» the words «with his lips?»

The Gemara answers: «As we found at» Mount «Sinai.» There one who had sexual relations with a woman was required to immerse himself before receiving the Torah, which was spoken and not merely contemplated. Here, too, it was decreed that one who was impure due to a seminal emission may not recite matters of Torah out loud until he immerses himself.

segments.he: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר, הִרְהוּר לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי — יוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו.
segments.en: «And Rav Ḥisda said» that the opposite conclusion should be drawn from the mishna: «Contemplation is not tantamount to speech, as if it would enter your mind» that «contemplation is tantamount to speech,» then one who is impure because of a seminal emission should ab initio, «utter» Shema «with his lips.»

segments.he: אֶלָּא מַאי הִרְהוּר לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי, לָמָּה מְהַרְהֵר? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ כׇּל הָעוֹלָם עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ וְהוּא יוֹשֵׁב וּבָטֵל.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this argument: «But what» are you saying, that «contemplation is not tantamount to speech?» If so, «why does he contemplate? Rabbi Elazar said: So that» a situation «will not» arise «where everyone is engaged in» reciting Shema «and he sits idly» by.

segments.he: וְנִגְרוֹס בְּפִרְקָא אַחֲרִינָא! אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: If that is the only purpose, «let him study another chapter» and not specifically Shema or one of the blessings. «Rav Adda bar Ahava said:» It is fitting that one engage «in a matter in which the community is engaged.»

segments.he: וַהֲרֵי תְּפִלָּה, דְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר עֲסוּקִין בּוֹ, וּתְנַן: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי — לֹא יַפְסִיק, אֶלָּא יְקַצֵּר. טַעְמָא דְּאַתְחֵיל, הָא לָא אַתְחֵיל — לֹא יַתְחִיל!
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «And prayer,» which is also «a matter in which the community is engaged, and we learned» in the mishna: «One who was standing in prayer and remembered that he is one» who experienced «a seminal emission» and did not yet immerse himself «should not interrupt» his prayer, «rather he should abridge it.» The Gemara infers: «The reason is because he» already «began» to pray; «however,» if «he did not» yet «begin,» then «he should not begin,» even by means of contemplation.

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי תְּפִלָּה דְּלֵית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם. וַהֲרֵי בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאַחֲרָיו דְּלֵית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, וּתְנַן עַל הַמָּזוֹן מְבָרֵךְ לְאַחֲרָיו וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ לְפָנָיו! אֶלָּא: קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וּתְפִלָּה דְּרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Prayer is different» in «that it does not contain» the acceptance of the yoke of «the kingdom of Heaven.» The Gemara rejects this: «And Grace after Meals does not contain» the acceptance of the yoke of «the kingdom of Heaven, and» yet «we learned» in the mishna: «Over food, one recites a blessing afterward, but does not recite a blessing beforehand. Rather,» the differences must be explained otherwise: «The recitation of Shema and Grace after Meals» are both mitzvot «by Torah law, while prayer» is only «by rabbinic law.» Therefore, one who is impure need not pray.

moves.summary: From the mishna: contemplation counts as speech; otherwise why would the ba'al keri contemplate?
moves.about: since the mishna has the ba'al keri contemplate Shema, contemplation must count as speech

moves.summary: If contemplation counts as speech, let him utter Shema with his lips.
moves.about: if contemplation counts as speech, the ba'al keri should simply utter Shema with his lips

moves.summary: As at Sinai: the impure may not speak Torah aloud, though contemplation is permitted.
moves.about: as at Sinai, one impure through emission may not speak Torah aloud but may contemplate it

moves.summary: The opposite inference: contemplation is not speech; otherwise he should utter it with his lips.
moves.about: since the mishna does not have the ba'al keri utter Shema, contemplation must not count as speech

moves.cueHe: אלא מאי הרהור לאו כדבור דמי
moves.summary: If contemplation is not speech, why does he contemplate at all?
moves.about: if contemplation is not speech, why does the ba'al keri contemplate at all

moves.summary: So that he not sit idle while everyone is engaged in Shema.
moves.about: he contemplates so that he not sit idle while everyone else is engaged in Shema

moves.summary: Then let him study some other chapter.
moves.about: if the point is only not to sit idle, let him study another chapter rather than Shema

moves.summary: He engages in the matter the community is engaged in.
moves.about: he should engage in the very matter the community is engaged in

moves.summary: Prayer is communal too, yet the mishna implies one who has not begun does not begin.
moves.about: prayer is also a communal matter, yet the mishna implies a ba'al keri who has not begun praying does not begin even by contemplation

moves.summary: Mishna: one standing in prayer who remembers he is a ba'al keri does not interrupt but abridges.
moves.about: one standing in prayer who remembers he is a ba'al keri does not interrupt but abridges

moves.summary: Only because he began; had he not begun, he would not begin.
moves.about: 'should not interrupt' implies only one who began continues; one who has not begun does not begin

moves.summary: Prayer differs: it has no acceptance of the kingdom of Heaven.
moves.about: prayer differs in that it contains no acceptance of the kingdom of Heaven

moves.summary: Grace after Meals also lacks it, yet the mishna has him bless after food.
moves.about: Grace after Meals also lacks acceptance of the kingdom of Heaven, yet the mishna has the ba'al keri bless after food

moves.summary: Mishna: over food he blesses afterward but not before.
moves.about: over food he blesses afterward but not before

moves.cueHe: אלא: קריאת שמע וברכת המזון דאורייתא
moves.summary: Rather: Shema and Grace after Meals are Torah law, prayer is rabbinic, so the impure need not pray.
moves.about: Shema and Grace after Meals are Torah obligations while prayer is rabbinic, so the impure need not pray
